comment: Canonical licensing table for King's Taster. Only sources listed here are described publicly. List-file fetchers may only use rows with use=list_file and in_list_file=true. Checked on 2026-11-27 against each source's published terms.

sources.attribution: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. No endorsement by CISA or DHS is implied. No CISA logo or DHS seal is used.

sources.source: OpenSSF Malicious Packages (MAL- records) via the OSV.dev export, npm
sources.redistribution: yes, with a copy of the license

sources.source: OpenSSF Malicious Packages (MAL- records) via the OSV.dev export, PyPI
sources.redistribution: yes, with a copy of the license

sources.source: GitHub Advisory Database content inside MAL- records whose origin is ghsa-malware
sources.license: CC-BY 4.0 (those entries also carry Apache-2.0 from OpenSSF)

sources.source: Google Safe Browsing canonicalization test vectors (in conformance.json)

sources.license: NIST publications are in the public domain in the United States under 17 U.S.C. § 105; NVD API terms also apply
sources.commercial_use: yes, with the required notice and no claim of endorsement
sources.redistribution: yes; if the API content is modified, do not attribute the modified content to the NVD
sources.attribution: This product uses data from the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD.
sources.key_needed: optional; a key raises the rate limit
sources.rate_limit: 5 requests in a rolling 30-second window without a key; 50 with a key (nvd.nist.gov/developers, checked 2026-11-27)

sources.source: Google Safe Browsing API v5 (live lookup)
sources.license: Google Safe Browsing and Google APIs terms
sources.commercial_use: no (Safe Browsing is for non-commercial use only; Google points commercial use to the Web Risk API)
sources.attribution: none required beyond the terms; lookups never enter the list file
sources.key_needed: yes; each user adds their own key
sources.rate_limit: a default quota is assigned in Google Developer Console (no single public number); urls.search accepts at most 50 URLs per request

sources.commercial_use: yes, for documented Public API use
sources.redistribution: do not redistribute npm security or audit data as part of other products; live metadata lookups are not copied into the list file
sources.attribution: none required for a live package-name lookup
sources.rate_limit: no published per-hour cap for the Public API; terms forbid an unreasonable volume, and state that five million requests in a month is never reasonable

sources.source: Python Package Index (pypi.org) JSON and Index APIs
sources.commercial_use: yes, subject to the Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy
sources.redistribution: live metadata lookups are not copied into the list file; do not use PyPI data for spam or to sell personal information
sources.attribution: none required for a live package-name lookup
sources.rate_limit: no published numeric edge limit for the JSON or Index APIs (checked 2026-11-27); identify the client with a User-Agent; do not send thousands of requests in a few minutes

sources.redistribution: live repo metadata is not copied into the list file
sources.attribution: none required for a live owner/name lookup
sources.key_needed: optional; a token with no special scopes raises the limit for public data
sources.rate_limit: 60 requests an hour without a token, counted by originating IP address; 5,000 an hour with a personal access token (docs.github.com, checked 2026-11-27). Whether several bots share one outgoing IP has not been measured.

sources.source: IANA RDAP bootstrap file and RDAP servers
sources.license: IANA protocol-parameter registries are dedicated to the public domain and licensed under CC0 1.0; each RDAP server may have its own terms
sources.commercial_use: yes, for the IANA bootstrap file
sources.redistribution: the bootstrap file may be redistributed under CC0; live RDAP answers are not copied into the list file
sources.attribution: none required for the IANA bootstrap file under CC0
sources.rate_limit: none published for the bootstrap file; RDAP servers set their own limits
